prompts: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one isolated transparent wooden rudder blade game sprite for a strict-overhead painted wooden dinghy. Input 1 is only a material/style reference (honey oak, restrained painted grain). Input 2 shows the boat's old timber finish. Generate ONLY ONE blade, no tiller, no hull, no hardware, no stock knob, no screws. Horizontal blade: RIGHT is the hinge/root, LEFT is the aft tip. Full blade length about 4.5 times maximum width. Root at right is a short narrow wooden neck; immediately to its left develop a clear broad gently curved shoulder. Blade then tapers smoothly toward a rounded narrower aft tip on left. Symmetric outline across the horizontal centerline. This is a stylized overhead silhouette for readability, broader than a literal edge-on deployed blade. Keep the surface visually mostly flat and wooden, restrained bevel highlights along edges, warm worn honey oak with darker edges, matching reference painterly style. DO NOT create a long narrow pole, rod, rounded stick, baseball bat, oar, or large circular paddle. No perspective tilt or foreshortening. The distinct wide shoulder and tapered blade should be readable at tiny game scale. Center one horizontal blade on a truly transparent wide canvas, filling about 90 percent of canvas width, with generous transparent margin all around. No cast shadow outside silhouette, no text, no background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: transparent painted wooden boat component sprite atlas. Input image 1 is the edit target: keep this exact broad tapered honey-oak rudder blade as the TOP ROW sprite, maintaining its shape, orientation and grain. Input image 2 supplies reference painted wood and aged bronze materials. Add a SECOND separate sprite in a new row below the blade, with a large transparent gap. This second sprite is a compact rudder hinge support: strict orthographic straight overhead view, rectangular honey-oak backing block with rounded corners, horizontal long axis, dark beveled edges. On its top a small aged bronze mounting plate with TWO small screw heads on its RIGHT half and one circular bearing/bore on the LEFT half. The bearing center must sit INSIDE the block footprint, about one third of block length from its left end, with visible supporting WOOD all around it (especially to the left of bearing); do not let the ring hang over the block edge. Block length120 millimeters, width65 millimeters; bronze bearing diameter30 millimeters. This block will bridge the outer transom edge with most of its length supported inside the boat. Warm old honey oak and modest dull bronze matching reference, restrained painted highlights and wear. Keep the block distinctly small, about one quarter of the top blade's image length. The blade's physical length450 millimeters. No tiller, no hull, no extra pole, no text, no labels, no scene, no cast shadow outside silhouettes. Both disconnected sprites centered horizontally, full sprites visible with generous transparent margins. Preserve genuine alpha transparency. Same exact strict overhead game perspective for both objects.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image is edit target, a transparent two-sprite atlas. KEEP THE TOP RUDDER BLADE EXACTLY AS IT IS, same silhouette, grain, position, scale and orientation. CHANGE ONLY LOWER MOUNTING BLOCK: make its wooden base much taller vertically, with an almost square outline, approximately 1.2 times as wide horizontally as tall vertically. The little base is 120mm long x100mm wide, seen strict vertical overhead. Keep the bronze ring at the left third of the block and the two bronze screw heads on its right half. IMPORTANT: the ring diameter is 45mm, less than half the block height, and visible honey-oak support WOOD must surround its entire circumference, with broad timber margins above and below the ring. The mounting block must look like a squat broad wooden support with a small bronze ring and short plate on top, not a long narrow tab. Let the block occupy more of the lower transparent margin and extend canvas height if needed, while keeping its upper edge safely separated from the upper rudder blade. Same warm old painted honey-oak and bronze finish. Transparent background, no shadows outside either silhouette, no third object, no text.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Pure SPRITE ATLAS LAYOUT correction only. Keep BOTH painted wooden objects and their shapes/materials exactly. The top long tapered rudder blade and lower compact wooden/bronze hinge block must have at least 150 pixels of completely transparent VERTICAL SPACE between their full bounding rectangles. Increase the image canvas HEIGHT to provide that empty gap; do not shrink, rotate, distort or redesign either object. Center each object horizontally in its own row. Top blade remains horizontal with narrow root at right. Lower block remains strict overhead with bearing left and screws right. Entire two objects visible with at least40px transparent outer margin. True transparent background. No new objects, no cast shadows, no text.
presentation: The broad blade is a stylized overhead silhouette for readability, not a physical projection of the deployed vertical blade.
